ii. Three (3) charge-sheet witnesses had not been examined by prosecution and non examination of charge-sheet witnesses gave rise to a presumption against the prosecution case. 

 23. One of the cardinal principles which has always to be kept in view in our system of administration of justice for criminal cases is that a person arraigned as an accused is presumed to be innocent unless that presumption is rebutted by prosecution on production of evidence as may show him to be guilty of the offence with which he is charged. Burden of proving the guilt of the accused' is upon the prosecution and unless it relieves itself of that burden, court cannot record a finding of the guilt of accused.
